newsitem.title: USA: READER'S DIGEST CHAIRMAN SCHADT RESIGNS.
newsitem.headline: READER'S DIGEST CHAIRMAN SCHADT RESIGNS.

text.p: Reader's Digest Association Inc said Monday its chairman and chief executive officer, James Schadt, has resigned.
A committee comprising independent directors has been formed to conduct the search for a permanent successor for the 59-year-old Schadt, it said.
Reader's Digest said that in the transition, former chief executive officer and chairman George Grune, who is 68, will act as chairman and CEO, effective immediately.

Grune led Reader's Digest efforts to transform itself from a private to a publicly-held company. The company said that during his decade at the company's helm, its revenues doubled and operating profit increased ninefold.
It said the board's committee that will seek out Schadt's replacement will be led by James Preston, chairman and CEO of Avon Products Inc.
The committee will include Walter Shipley, chairman and CEO of Chase Manhattan Corp, and Willliam White, chairman of Bell & Howell Co, it said.
The company gave no reason for Schadt's resignation and a spokeswoman was not immediately available to comment.
Earlier this year, the company announced a four-year $400 million program to aggressively promote its products after experiencing an earnings slump.

About a month ago, the company reduced its quarterly dividend to $0.225, from $0.45. It also said it expected earnings per share for the fiscal year ended June 30 to be $1.20, including fourth quarter charges in a range of $0.20 to $0.25 a share.
It blamed the situation on the unusually big difference between actual customer response to its third and fourth quarter promotional mailings compared with expected response.
